question: How can a RAG system detect and correct retrieval that returns irrelevant documents, rather than feeding them to the generator?
hypothesis: A lightweight trained retrieval evaluator that triggers refinement, web search or both will make RAG and Self-RAG more robust to bad retrieval.
contributions: First attempt to design corrective strategies for RAG when the retriever returns inaccurate results
A plug-and-play method named CRAG for self-correction and efficient use of retrieved documents
Experiments showing adaptability to RAG-based approaches and generalizability across short- and long-form generation

method.summary: A fine-tuned T5-large scores each (question, document) pair; the scores trigger Correct (refine documents into filtered strips), Incorrect (discard and use rewritten-query web search) or Ambiguous (both). The result feeds a frozen generator; coupled to RAG (CRAG) and to Self-RAG (Self-CRAG).
method.task: retrieval-augmented generation: short-form QA, long-form biography, true/false, multiple choice

datasets.name: PopQA
datasets.split: 1,399 test (Self-RAG split); remainder used to fine-tune the evaluator
datasets.source: Mallen et al. 2023; golden subject wiki title used as positive relevance signal
datasets.preprocessing: positives label 1, negatives -1 randomly sampled from retrieval results

models.name: Contriever
models.architecture: dense retriever; Self-RAG's retrieval results reused

other.use: query rewriting and as a prompted retrieval evaluator baseline

training.objective: fine-tune evaluator as relevance scorer, labels +1 / -1

other.note: evaluator fine-tuned on PopQA only (the PopQA samples left after the 1,399 test queries), transferred to Bio, Pub, ARC

inference.samples: inferred: single run per cell, no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: ChatGPT rewrites question to at most three keywords with a 4-shot prompt (Table 7)
inference.retrieval: top documents from Contriever as given by Self-RAG; Google Search API top-k 5, Wikipedia pages preferred

parameters.Correct rule: at least one document above upper threshold

eval.protocol: Numbers for non-CRAG baselines cited from original papers except starred (*) reproductions; no seeds, variance or significance test.

availability.data: public datasets; PopQA from huggingface akariasai/PopQA

prompts.text: Extract at most three keywords separated by comma from the following dialogues and questions as queries for the web search, including topic background within dialogues and main intent within questions.
prompts.where: Appendix A, Table 7 (4 few-shot examples follow)

prompts.text: Given a question, does the following document have exact information to answer the question? Answer yes or no only.

limits: Fine-tuning an external retrieval evaluator is required (authors concede).
Evaluator is trained on PopQA only and transferred; thresholds were set empirically per dataset, with no stated tuning procedure.
All generators are LLaMA2-7B variants; no larger or proprietary generator.
Single run per cell, no variance or significance.
Table 6 overhead excludes retrieval and web search stages.
Self-RAG and Self-CRAG on LLaMA2-hf-7b PubHealth score under 1 owing to output-format failure, so those gains are not meaningful.
Evaluator accuracy (Table 4) does not define how ground-truth retrieval correctness is labeled.
Google Search dependence limits reproducibility over time.

terms.definition: Three actions triggered by evaluator confidence against upper and lower thresholds
Split documents into strips, score each with the evaluator, filter, concatenate the kept strips in order
